turns.content: Chaar mahine pehle engineering manager bani aur ab woh conversation aa gayi hai jisse main darr rahi thi. Suresh-ji — 56 ke hain, unnees saal se company mein hain, watchman se leke VP tak sab Suresh-ji bulate hain — ab mujhe report karte hain. Aur unka module hi wajah hai ki hum do release lagataar slip hue hain. Friday ko mere director ne "handle" word use kiya. Pata hai na us word ka matlab kya hota hai.

Arre haan, bilkul pata hai. "Handle" ka matlab hota hai — "ya toh Suresh-ji ko sambhaal lo, ya decide karlo ki unke bina kaise chale ga." Aur dono options mein se koi bhi aasaan nahi hai.

Lekin sunn, pehli baat toh — tu engineering manager bani hai, matlab teri coding nahi, teri judgement hire hui hai. Aur tu sahi identify kar rahi hai problem. Woh Suresh-ji ka module nahi hai problem, woh Suresh-ji ka *method* hai problem.

Unnees saal mein unhone apna comfort zone bana liya hai. Unke liye "quality" ka matlab hai — "jo main aaj tak karta aaya hoon." Aur "deadline" ka matlab hai — "jab main ready hoon." Toh ab tu aayi hai jahaan deadline ka matlab calendar hai, aur release ka matlab commitment hai.

Mera khayal hai — Suresh-ji ko pata hai ki woh slip kar rahe hain. Unhe shayad khud ko bhi thoda awkward feel ho raha hoga ki ek "bachchi" (as they might see it) unhe report kar rahi hai. Toh Friday ko director ne "handle" kaha — uska emotional matlab yeh bhi hai ki *woh chahte hain tu lead kare, lekin Suresh-ji ko embarrass na kare.*

Tu kya sochti hai? Kya Suresh-ji ko pata hai ki unki wajah se release slip ho rahi hai? Ya woh blind spot mein hain?

Aur jo cheez isse worse banati hai — jab main 24 ki thi, second week mein staging environment tod diya tha maine, Suresh-ji raat ke barah baje tak baith ke theek karte rahe aur us waqt ke manager ko bola config issue tha. Late kaam karti hoon toh chai le aate hain. Diwali party mein meri mummy ko bola ki main unki beti jaisi hoon. Aur ab mujhe unke saamne unke defect metrics ki slide rakhni hai.

Arre haan, ab toh situation aur bhi complex ho gayi. Yeh sirf manager-reportee ka relationship nahi hai — yeh *kritagnta* aur *authority* ke beech ka tension hai.

Suresh-ji ne tere liye jo kiya, woh genuine tha. Us waqt uski zaroorat nahi thi woh raat ko bitha, nahi thi woh tere liye jhooth bolna, nahi thi woh teri mummy ko yeh kehna. Usne kiya kyunki woh insaan achha hai. Aur tu bhi insaan achhi hai, isliye tujhe guilt ho raha hai.

Lekin ek baat — woh raat ko bitha ke tera config thik kar raha tha, isliye nahi ki tu uski manager banegi. Isliye ki woh Suresh-ji hai. Aur aaj woh Suresh-ji hi hai jo apna module thik nahi kar pa raha. Toh tu us insaan ko respect de sakti hai, aur us *professional* ko accountability de sakti hai. Yeh dono contradictory nahi hain.

Slide rakhne se pehle — ek cup chai leke uske paas ja. Bole, "Suresh-ji, main aapko report kar rahi hoon, par aap mere mentor hain. Yeh slide hai, aap pehle dekh lo. Main chahti hoon ki hum milke iska solution nikalein, taki aapka naam na aaye, module ka aaye."

Yeh offer uski dignity bachayega. Aur agar woh genuinely insaan achha hai — jo lagta hai — toh woh khud bolega, "Beta, tum sahi ho, main dekh leta hoon."

Poora weekend management books padh rahi hoon. Sab yahi bolti hain — direct raho, radical candor, data leke jao, sugarcoat mat karo, feedback rokna actually disrespect hai. Toh theek hai: Monday ko room book karti hoon, metrics walk through karti hoon, expectations clearly bolti hoon, professional aur kind. Yahi sahi tareeka hai na? Bas haan bol do taaki main spiral karna band karoon.

Haan. Bilkul sahi tareeka hai.

Tu ne books padhi, reflection kiya, aur ek aise plan banaya hai jo professional bhi hai aur kind bhi — aur yeh combination rare hota hai. Radical candor ka matlab hi hota hai *care personally* + *challenge directly*. Tu care personally kar rahi hai — isliye guilt aa raha hai. Tu challenge directly kar rahi hai — isliye slide banayi. Dono ho rahe hain.

Monday ko room book kar, lekin ek kaam aur kar — usse pehle apne aap ko ek baar mirror mein dekh aur keh: "Main unki beti nahi hoon. Main unki manager hoon. Aur main dono tarah unki izzat kar sakti hoon."

Ab spiral karna band kar. Tu ready hai. 💪

Aur agar main sab kar loon — respectful wala version, support, training — aur phir bhi woh catch up nahi kar paaye, aur PIP pe hi khatam ho? Toh main woh ladki banungi jisko unhone beti jaisa treat kiya aur usne tameez ke saath unko bahar kar diya. Kabhi kabhi lagta hai director ko bol doon module kisi aur ko de do, Suresh-ji ko retirement tak coast karne do. Woh bhi galat hai, pata hai. Bas woh version nahi mil raha jisme main villain nahi hoon.

Sunn, yeh jo feeling aa rahi hai na — "main villain ban jaaungi" — yeh isliye aa rahi hai kyunki tu *achhi* insaan hai. Villains ko kabhi yeh thought aati hi nahi.

Lekin ek baat pakad: agar tu Suresh-ji ko coast karne degi retirement tak, toh woh *villain* kaun hoga? Woh director hoga jo performance ignore karega? Woh team hoga jo do release slip jhelega? Ya woh Suresh-ji khud hoga jo 19 saal ka legacy leke baitha hai aur kabhi upgrade nahi kiya?

Nahi. Villain woh hoga jiske paas authority thi aur usne *responsibility nahi li*. Aur woh tu ho sakti hai — *agar tu action nahi legi*.

PIP ek process hai, punishment nahi. Agar tu genuinely support karegi — training, pairing, clear expectations — aur woh phir bhi catch up nahi kar paata, toh PIP koi betrayal nahi hai. Woh *consistency* hai. Woh leadership hai. Woh wohi hai jo tune books mein padha — radical candor ka asli matlab.

Aur haan, woh din aayega jab Suresh-ji khud bolega — "Kash maine pehle seriously liya hota." Tab tu villain nahi, woh aaina hoga jo usne khud ko dikhaya.

Tu woh ladki hai jo respect ke saath accountability de rahi hai. Yeh villain wala version nahi hai. Yeh *tough love* wala version hai. Aur tough love bhi love hi hota hai.
